subject: 4D23BC811AC9E800B36CF057A7209E03
introduction: People wrote to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about their dreams, and he answered. These readings are those answers, with a few of Bahá’u’lláh’s: a star and fish, a ladder, milk, a sealed paper, a tree, a flood in the house. Read together they show a method. Symbols mean different things in different dreams; some dreams are to be read by opposites, so that weeping is joy; some need no interpretation; some are fancy. An interpretation may have to wait: “the time … has not yet come.” And nearly every reading turns the dream toward the dreamer’s growth or service and away from prediction. The biblical interpreters, Joseph and Daniel, work the same way, part by part, and both insist the meaning is not theirs to give; Jesus explains a parable as ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains a dream. The Qur’án’s vision of Mecca is cited in the readings themselves. Homer’s two gates, Ben Sira’s warning, Bacon’s remark that we count the hits and forget the misses, Plato’s “wild-beast nature” and Freud’s wish-fulfilment give the other accounts of what a dream is.
questions: In these answers the same symbol can mean different things for different people. What does that suggest about how the interpretation was reached?
“The time for the interpretation of the dream has not yet come.” When is it wiser to keep a dream, as Jacob and Mary kept what they could not yet understand, than to explain it?
Most of the interpretations point to the dreamer’s growth or service. Why might ‘Abdu’l-Bahá have turned dreams in that direction and not toward foretelling events?
Freud saw wishes in dreams and Plato saw the “wild beast.” The readings distinguish true dreams from those “mixed with impressions of the heart.” How would you tell which kind you had had?
Bacon says we remember the dreams that came true and forget the rest. How should that caution affect the way a believer uses the practice shown here?

outside.why: A dream of a star and of clouds turned into fish is read as the appearance of the Promised One. Joseph, asked to interpret: do not interpretations belong to God?
The Bible’s great example of a symbol read part by part: this is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof. Thou, O king, art this head of gold.
Clear water and fish are “most auspicious.” Joseph before Pharaoh: the seven good kine are seven years; and the seven thin and ill favoured kine are seven years of famine.
The fish are souls, to be drawn out “with the net of the love of God.” Jesus to two fishermen: follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
“The time for the interpretation of the dream has not yet come.” Habakkuk: the vision is yet for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it.
Jacob rebuked his son’s dream and still kept it in mind: his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
Ascent from earth to heaven means “growth in the love of God.” Jacob’s dream: a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven.
A sun seen in a dream is the Promised One. Joseph in the Qur’án: I saw in a dream eleven planets and the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating themselves unto me.
“Drinking milk symbolizes knowledge and wisdom.” Peter uses the same figure awake: as newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word.
Each item of the dream is given its meaning in turn. Jesus explains a parable the same way: the field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; the harvest is the end of the world.
Dreams are read “in the contraries and opposites, for laughter in the world of vision is weeping, and weeping, joy.” Jesus: blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
A dream left a woman tearful and afraid, and consolation did not help. Pilate’s wife: I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
“We shall interpret it for thee as a bounty from Us.” Daniel disclaims any skill of his own: there is a God in heaven that revealeth secrets.
“We are commanded to look to the outward, not the inward.” Moses: the secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us.

The servant’s “vision of the fiery horses” is named among spiritual discoveries. The passage: the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire.
And “Peter’s vision.” Peter himself gives its interpretation: God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.

“True dreams, dreams requiring interpretation, and confused dreams and fancies.” Penelope: those that come through the gate of ivory are fatuous, but those from the gate of horn mean something to those that see them.

Freud, a few years before these letters were written, proposed one key for all dreams: the dream is the fulfilment of a wish. The second kind of dream, “mixed with impressions of the heart,” comes nearest to his. What does his theory explain, and what in the readings could it not account for?

Plato thought dreams show what is worst in us: in all of us, even in good men, there is a lawless wild-beast nature, which peers out in sleep. The readings find in dreams what is best. Could both be right about different dreams?
A vision in prayer is “evidence of spiritual nearness.” Luke on how such things are best held: Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
A cable foretold visitors before they were known to be coming. Paul was directed by a vision of a man of Macedonia, and immediately we endeavoured to go.
A child’s dream is told to his father and an interpreter is called. Joseph told his: the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
A dream of danger approaching by sea, later understood. Joseph of Nazareth was warned in a dream: arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt.
Pharaoh’s dream was a warning with a use: let them lay up corn, and that food shall be for store against the seven years of famine.
A victory promised in a dream was delayed, “some were overcome with doubt,” and then Mecca was entered. The Qur’án on that dream: Allah hath fulfilled the vision for His messenger in very truth.

So many dreams were sent for interpretation that answers had to be brief. Ben Sira would have discouraged the letters: whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind. What keeps attention to dreams from becoming what he describes?

Bacon on why interpretations seem to succeed: men mark when they hit, and never mark when they miss; as they do generally also of dreams. Most of these interpretations concern the dreamer’s growth and service, which cannot “miss” in his sense. Is that a weakness or the point?
A paper seen in a dream that could not be read: “thou shalt read it.” Isaiah: the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed.
“Wash and then touch.” The dream’s command is read as inner cleansing. Elisha to Naaman: go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thou shalt be clean.
Tablets dripping water are the teachings, “from which the water of life drips.” Jesus: out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.
A mighty tree with roots in earth and branches in heaven. Nebuchadnezzar’s dream: I saw, and behold a tree in the midst of the earth, and the height thereof reached unto heaven.
High steps are “lofty spiritual stations.” Jacob, waking: surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not.
Some will try to put out the Fire and only make it greater. A soldier’s dream of a barley loaf overturning a tent, and his comrade’s reading: this is nothing else save the sword of Gideon.
“As for the weeping, it is joy.” The psalm: they that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
A dream means “new seed-sowing and fresh teaching work.” Jesus: behold, a sower went forth to sow.
One who saw ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in a dream “didst arise to serve.” Isaiah, after his vision: here am I; send me.
A vision that should shape waking conduct. The psalmist: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.
Meeting him in a dream “indicates the purity of your inner being.” Jesus: blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
“Give thanks unto God for having revealed Himself unto thee” in a dream. Elihu: in a dream, in a vision of the night, he openeth the ears of men.
“The time for dream interpretation has come—both in wakefulness and in dreams.” Peter at Pentecost: your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.

shortfall: Most of the 73 readings are replies to individuals, each interpreting one person’s dream; many are a sentence long and many give the same assurance. The guide is read with 40 outside quotations, placed where they show a like symbol, a like method, or a doubt; none was added only to reach the number of 79.

judges-barley-bread-tumbled-into-the-hos.text: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man that told a dream unto his fellow, and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the host of Midian, and came unto a tent, and smote it that it fell, and overturned it, that the tent lay along. And his fellow answered and said, This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: for into his hand hath God delivered Midian, and all the host

matthew-the-field-is-the-world.text: He answered and said unto them, He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels

genesis-seven-good-kine-are-seven-years.text: And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: God hath shewed Pharaoh what he is about to do. The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one. And the seven thin and ill favoured kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine

genesis-his-father-observed-the-saying.text: And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying

daniel-thou-art-this-head-of-gold.text: This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king. Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory. And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold

freud-dream-is-the-fulfilment-of-a-wish.text: The Dream is the Fulfilment of a Wish
